record.title: Dragon Ball: Sparking! ZERO [Switch 2]
record.description:
DRAGON BALL: Sparking! ZERO revives the arena-brawler structure associated with the Budokai Tenkaichi series. The base game features more than 180 fighters from Dragon Ball Z, Dragon Ball Super, Dragon Ball GT and selected films, with transformations, signature techniques and large destructible battle arenas.

Episode Battle revisits major story conflicts from the viewpoints of several fighters and includes branching scenarios. Custom Battle allows players to build and share their own encounters. The Nintendo Switch 2 version supports local play, local wireless and online multiplayer, as well as motion-control options using Joy-Con controllers.

record.tagline: Bring Dragon Ball’s biggest clashes to life with a huge roster, explosive 3D arenas, transformations, Episode Battle and player-created Custom Battles.
fitFor: Dragon Ball fans who want a huge roster covering many eras, transformations and signature techniques.
Players who enjoy fast 3D arena fighting rather than traditional 2D fighting-game lanes.
Players who want both story recreations and custom/online battle formats.
notFitFor: Players looking for a deep exploration RPG rather than a dedicated fighting game.
Players who prefer slow, highly technical 2D tournament fighters with small tightly balanced rosters.

gameplayPillars.title: High-Speed 3D Combat
gameplayPillars.description: Fly, dash, counter, transform and unleash signature attacks across large arenas designed to reproduce the scale and spectacle of Dragon Ball battles.

gameplayPillars.title: Massive Character Roster
gameplayPillars.description: Choose from more than 180 base-game fighters, including multiple forms and eras from Z, Super, GT and the films.

gameplayPillars.title: Episode and Custom Battles
gameplayPillars.description: Replay famous confrontations through character-focused Episode Battles or build original what-if scenarios with Custom Battle tools.

record.worldSummary: Sparking! ZERO is not built around one explorable overworld. Instead, it recreates locations and battles from across the Dragon Ball timeline as large 3D combat arenas. Episode Battle revisits major events through selected character perspectives, while Custom Battle lets players construct and share alternative match scenarios and conditions.

storyChapters.title: Episode Battle Perspectives
storyChapters.body: The story mode follows major Dragon Ball events from the perspective of eight playable characters rather than using one single continuous protagonist.

storyChapters.title: Iconic Sagas and What-If Paths
storyChapters.body: Battles revisit recognizable conflicts while selected choices and conditions can lead to alternate Sparking Episode outcomes.

storyChapters.title: Custom Battle Creation
storyChapters.body: Beyond the official scenarios, Custom Battle allows players to configure characters, conditions and presentation to create their own Dragon Ball match stories.

features: The base game includes more than 180 playable fighters drawn from Dragon Ball Z, Dragon Ball Super, Dragon Ball GT and selected films.
High-speed 3D arena battles feature transformations, beam clashes, rush attacks and large-scale signature techniques.
Episode Battle retells major story conflicts from the perspectives of eight characters and also includes alternate encounters.
Custom Battle lets players create, play and share custom scenarios and dream matchups.
The Nintendo versions support local multiplayer, local wireless and online play, with player counts depending on the mode.
Joy-Con motion controls are supported on Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 versions for an alternative control style.
record.perfNotes: Bandai Namco’s platform comparison reports a maximum 810p presentation using dynamic resolution and 30 FPS in both docked and portable modes on Nintendo Switch 2, with HDR support. Nintendo Life’s later review confirms the 30 FPS cap and notes some performance issues.

devicePerformance.performanceNotes: Official comparison information reports dynamic resolution up to 810p and 30 FPS in both Switch 2 play modes, with HDR supported.

faq.a: Nintendo and Bandai Namco describe more than 180 fighters in the base game, spanning multiple Dragon Ball eras and transformations.

faq.q: Does the game have paid DLC?
faq.a: Yes. Official paid content includes a Season Pass and character packs tied to Dragon Ball Super: SUPER HERO and Dragon Ball DAIMA, among other additions.
Episode Battle recreates major Dragon Ball story events from the viewpoints of selected characters, with some branches and alternate outcomes.

record.verdictSummary:
Score note: 7.8/10 is a direct normalization of the current 78/100 Metacritic aggregate for the Nintendo listing; it is not a separately invented store rating.

Sparking! ZERO prioritizes Dragon Ball spectacle and roster breadth over traditional fighting-game restraint. It is strongest for fans who want transformations, signature techniques and recognizable battles presented at large scale.
verdictPros: Huge roster with broad Dragon Ball era coverage.
Spectacular transformations and signature attacks in large 3D arenas.
Episode Battle and Custom Battle provide substantial single-player scenario variety.
verdictCons: Roster size can make competitive balance uneven.
Fast camera movement and visual effects can become chaotic.
Players seeking an exploration RPG will find the structure heavily battle-focused.
